title: A pre-emptive vaccine against diverse pandemic coronaviruses

concept.text: The proposed innovation is a vaccine that provides durable protection against substantially different coronaviruses before a new pandemic threat emerges. Its defining capability would be protection extending beyond the viruses used to design it, including genuinely divergent threats. This is a target capability, not an achievement established by the supplied evidence.

Scientific framing from the research notes: coronavirus spike variation makes breadth difficult, while antibody targets shared across viruses may be hard to expose or make dominant in the immune response. The intended vaccine would need to turn recognition of shared features into reliable protection across diverse threats. These are proposed scientific motivations; the retained source copies contain no scientific text with which to verify the specific mechanisms.

Conceptual distinction: breadth must be defined by both the viruses covered and the outcome protected against. Preventing severe disease, preventing symptomatic illness and preventing infection or onward transmission are different capabilities. The concept does not require assuming that success on one endpoint automatically establishes the others, or that coverage of selected coronavirus lineages establishes coverage of the entire family.

significance.text: Conditional impact: if a sufficiently broad and durable vaccine were deployed before a divergent coronavirus emerged, vaccinated people could enter the outbreak with useful protection already in place. This would change preparedness from relying entirely on a vaccine developed after identification to having some protection available at the beginning. The revolutionary element is advance protection against unfamiliar threats.

Conditional downstream possibilities depend on the protection achieved. Protection against severe disease could reduce clinical burden even if infections continued. Substantial protection against infection or transmission could also help constrain spread. These possibilities require separate evidence: broad neutralization alone would not establish either population-level outcome.

Limits on impact: a vaccine's availability would not create immediate population immunity. Benefits would depend on prior deployment, uptake, delivery, durability and effectiveness in the people exposed. Even successful coverage of a diverse test panel would not guarantee protection against every future coronavirus or establish that pandemics would be prevented. Pre-emptive breadth and rapid responses to newly identified threats would remain complementary capabilities.

missing_breakthrough.text: The target breakthrough is a reproducible way to elicit a durable protective immune response across known and genuinely divergent coronavirus threats. The supplied evidence does not establish how close the field is to this capability or whether it remains unachieved across all relevant approaches as of November 2026. That uncertainty concerns the state of the evidence, while the innovation's intended capability remains clear.

Proposed scientific barriers include selecting shared targets that remain useful across divergent viruses, presenting those targets so they reliably attract protective responses, and sustaining those responses over time. The research specifically identifies spike variation, conserved-target accessibility and immunological dominance as obstacles. Their importance in the particular reported vaccine approach cannot be verified from the retained copies.

Scientific reasoning: isolating an antibody with cross-lineage activity would demonstrate that a particular antibody can recognize and neutralize the tested viruses. It would not by itself demonstrate that vaccination regularly produces enough of that activity in the overall immune response, that the response persists, or that it protects an animal or person. Bridging those levels—from isolated antibodies to consistent serum activity to durable protection—is a central evidentiary and engineering requirement.

Proposed development barriers also include choosing a virus panel that meaningfully tests generalization, using appropriate protection models, and establishing safety and effectiveness across intended human populations. A panel concentrated around the design viruses could overstate breadth. Conversely, success against selected divergent viruses would establish useful demonstrated breadth without resolving performance against every untested threat.

current_state.text: The research notes attribute a nonhuman-primate study to Dueker and colleagues under the title “Heterologous betacoronavirus spike immunization in non-human primates elicits antibodies that neutralize both sarbeco- and merbecoviruses,” with a reported Cell Reports publication date of 3 June 2026 and DOI 10.1016/j.celrep.2026.117439. Those bibliographic details are carried forward as research-note attributions. The supplied review could not verify the document identity or publication details from the retained PubMed copy.

The same notes report rare isolated antibodies with cross-lineage neutralization following nonhuman-primate immunization, while describing the serum response as insufficient to establish broadly protective immunity. An earlier research pass additionally reported undetectable S2-directed serum cross-neutralization. Neither retained source contains scientific content substantiating antibody rarity, neutralization breadth, serum findings or S2 specificity. These remain reported findings requiring verification; the access failure does not show that they are false.

The research described the second PubMed item as a separate January 2026 preprint and stated that its abstract had been inspected. The supplied review found only a cookie-access notice in that retained copy, just as in the purported published record. Consequently, the retained evidence does not establish the second item's identity, date, preprint status or relationship to the reported publication. The earlier claim of an inspectable preprint abstract cannot be retained as a verified account of the available material.

Both retained PubMed artifacts were retrieved on 11 November 2026 and contain access notices rather than abstracts or full scientific text. The source index records saved, untruncated artifacts, but successful saving does not establish access to article content. No independently inspected published full text, verified quantitative performance results or demonstrated human protection can be established from these copies. The empty freshness record also leaves completeness of coverage through 1 November 2026 unresolved; retrieval on 11 November does not establish that the research was current.

completion_criteria.text: Proposed demonstration: human trials would establish an acceptable safety profile and durable protection against multiple circulating coronaviruses, using explicit clinical endpoints and a prespecified follow-up period. The development program would state whether its claim concerns severe disease, symptomatic illness, infection or transmission. These are proposed criteria for convincing evidence, not an established consensus standard; the supplied materials specify no justified numerical efficacy threshold or duration.
completion_criteria.label: Human trials establish acceptable safety and durable multi-coronavirus protection

completion_criteria.text: Proposed breadth demonstration: neutralization studies and appropriate animal-protection experiments would test a diverse, prespecified set of viruses excluded from vaccine design. Selection would explain which coronavirus lineages and degrees of divergence are represented and how exclusion tests generalization. Results would distinguish isolated antibody activity, serum neutralization and protection after challenge, with assay conditions and limitations made explicit.
completion_criteria.label: Breadth experiments demonstrate protection against prespecified viruses excluded from vaccine-design

completion_criteria.text: Proposed reproducibility requirement: independent laboratories would reproduce the central breadth findings, and further cohorts would show that protective responses occur consistently rather than only in exceptional individuals. Follow-up would assess persistence and the effect of additional doses. A credible interpretation would disclose unsuccessful tests and specify the populations, viruses, endpoints and observation periods for which protection was demonstrated.
completion_criteria.label: Independently reproduced breadth findings accompany consistent protective responses across cohorts

completion_criteria.text: Proposed practical boundary: the vaccine would need a feasible manufacturing and delivery regimen compatible with deployment before an outbreak. Evidence would identify any dependence on boosting and any limits in intended recipient groups. No finite experimental program could prove literal protection against every future coronavirus; completion would mean a clearly bounded, reproducible demonstration of broad and durable protection.
completion_criteria.label: Feasible manufacturing and delivery enable deployment before an outbreak

related_concepts.text: Roster-based comparison: INF-09, “A rapid, end-to-end vaccine response to a newly identified pathogen,” addresses speed after identification, whereas INF-08 addresses breadth established before emergence. They could reinforce one another if a pre-emptive vaccine supplied initial protection while a tailored response was developed. The supplied roster supports this title-level distinction, although no fuller INF-09 definition or evidence record is available here.

Roster-based comparison: INF-01, “A broadly protective HIV vaccine,” shares the ambition of protection despite viral diversity. INF-03, “A tuberculosis vaccine that interrupts transmission,” and INF-13, “A highly protective, durable and readily deliverable malaria vaccine,” overlap in vaccination, durability or deployment goals. Their pathogens and intended protection endpoints remain distinct; success in one would not establish success in another.

Roster-based comparison: INF-07, “Broad-spectrum treatment for unrelated viral infections,” also seeks breadth, but concerns treatment across unrelated viruses rather than pre-emptive vaccination within coronaviruses. INF-02, “A safe, scalable cure for established HIV infection,” INF-11, “A safe, broadly effective treatment-free cure for chronic hepatitis B,” and INF-12, “Very short, reliable curative treatment for active and latent tuberculosis,” concern curing established infections rather than supplying advance vaccine protection.

Roster-based comparison: INF-10, “Prevention of multiple sclerosis by controlling Epstein–Barr virus,” and INF-14, “Mechanism-guided prevention of major post-viral syndromes,” concern downstream consequences of viral infection. INF-08 could contribute to preventing such consequences only where its protection and the relevant disease pathway were demonstrated. Protection against acute coronavirus disease alone would not establish prevention of a post-viral syndrome.

Roster-based comparison: INF-04, “A reliable way to break malaria transmission through its vectors,” INF-05, “Near-patient diagnosis of the cause and treatability of most serious infections,” INF-06, “A dependable platform for generating new antibacterial treatments,” and INF-15, “A rapidly adaptable clinical phage-therapy platform,” are complementary infectious-disease capabilities. Their primary mechanisms—vector control, diagnosis, antibacterial development and phage therapy—remain separate from INF-08's pre-emptive vaccine breadth.

unresolved_issues: The reported Dueker study's identity, publication date, DOI and scientific findings remain unverified from the retained artifacts.
The second PubMed item's identity, alleged January 2026 preprint status and relationship to the reported publication remain unresolved.
Antibody rarity, cross-lineage neutralization, serum breadth and the reported absence of S2-directed serum cross-neutralization require inspectable scientific evidence.
The supplied material does not establish whether the target capability remains unachieved or whether research coverage is complete through 1 November 2026.
The intended coronavirus coverage, protection endpoints, durability period, target populations and acceptable performance thresholds remain unspecified.
A convincing held-out-virus panel and the relationship between its results, animal protection and human protection remain to be defined.
Related-concept comparisons are limited to the supplied roster titles; fuller definitions and evidence records were not provided.

brief.title: A vaccine against coronaviruses before they emerge
possible: People could enter a new coronavirus outbreak with protection already in place. A vaccine given beforehand would provide lasting protection even against substantially different viruses that were not used to design it.
why: Advance protection would give people a head start while a vaccine tailored to the new threat was developed. Protection against severe illness could ease pressure on hospitals. Protection against infection or spread could also help contain an outbreak.

sources.showed: Vaccinated macaques produced isolated antibodies, immune proteins that block viruses, active against distinct coronavirus groups. These protected animals against a test infection. Blood tests found no broad blocking activity targeting the shared region of the virus's surface protein.
sources.quote: These bnAbs neutralized diverse sarbeco- and merbecoviruses, including MERS-CoV, and conferred robust in vivo protection against SARS-CoV-2 challenge.
sources.cited_for: Vaccination can produce individual antibodies with activity across distinct coronavirus groups.
sources.not_established: Isolated protective antibodies do not establish that vaccination reliably produces lasting, broad protection in people.

sources.showed: An earlier version of the same work.

shown: Dueker and colleagues have demonstrated a protective ingredient in a macaque study. The remaining leap is for vaccination to produce enough broadly active antibodies throughout the immune response, keep them working over time, and protect against substantially different threats.
missing: Human trials still need to establish acceptable safety and lasting protection against multiple coronaviruses.
Protection must extend to diverse viruses excluded from vaccine design.
Independent teams must reproduce broad protection, with consistent responses across groups of recipients.
Manufacturing and delivery must support vaccination before an outbreak, including any repeat doses needed.

milestones.label: Human trials establish safety and lasting protection
milestones.explanation: Human trials would have to establish acceptable safety and lasting protection against multiple circulating coronaviruses, specifying which outcomes improve. This would establish a useful benefit for people.

milestones.label: Protection extends to viruses excluded from vaccine design
milestones.explanation: Laboratory tests and animal experiments would have to demonstrate protection against a diverse set of viruses chosen beforehand and excluded from vaccine design. This would test protection against unfamiliar threats.

milestones.label: Independent teams reproduce consistent protective responses
milestones.explanation: Independent laboratories would have to reproduce broad protection, while further groups of recipients show consistent, persistent responses. This would establish that success extends beyond exceptional individuals.

milestones.label: Manufacturing and delivery support vaccination before outbreaks
milestones.explanation: A feasible manufacturing and delivery programme would have to support advance vaccination, accounting for repeat doses and recipient limits. This would turn demonstrated protection into practical preparedness.

uncertain: The required virus coverage, duration of protection and acceptable level of benefit remain undefined.
Preventing severe illness, preventing infection and reducing spread are separate outcomes that need separate evidence.
How well tests against selected viruses predict human protection against future threats remains an open question.

page.title: Broadly protective betacoronavirus vaccine
page.definition: A vaccine given before exposure protects against severe disease for at least one year across sarbecoviruses and merbecoviruses—the coronavirus groups containing SARS and MERS viruses—including viruses whose antigens were absent from the vaccine.

goal.need: SARS-CoV, MERS-CoV and SARS-CoV-2 caused three epidemic or pandemic emergences within two decades. The coronavirus vaccine roadmap identifies advance protection against pre-emergent viruses as a preparedness goal and distinguishes routine vaccination from stockpiling vaccines for use after an outbreak begins.

completion.title: A vaccine receives a licence covering one-year protection across sarbecoviruses and merbecoviruses.
completion.criterion: A regulator licenses a vaccine for pre-exposure prevention of severe disease across sarbecoviruses and merbecoviruses, with protection lasting at least one year after the specified regimen. Accepted evidence supports protection against viruses whose antigens were absent from the vaccine, including pre-emergent animal coronaviruses. Human safety and efficacy evidence, together with any animal evidence or immune-response comparisons used to extend the breadth claim, supports that indication. This operational test is an Atlas fallback.
completion.set_by: Atlas synthesis of CIDRAP's breadth and duration objectives and the FDA vaccine licensing framework; no integrated external completion test was located.
completion.basis: WHO's COVID-19 product profile, NIAID's funding notice, CEPI's funding call and CIDRAP's roadmap were searched for a combined breadth, efficacy and durability test; none was found. CIDRAP supplies the one-year duration and sarbecovirus/merbecovirus scope. FDA supplies the licensing framework. This synthesis selects no efficacy percentage or virus-panel size. CIDRAP's landscape lists no approved broadly protective vaccine.

milestones.title: Vaccine-elicited antibodies neutralise a vaccine-absent coronavirus at the 50% assay endpoint.
milestones.criterion: Antibodies elicited by vaccination reach 50% neutralisation in a virus-entry assay against a coronavirus whose antigen was absent from the immunisation regimen. This is an assay endpoint, not an established protective antibody concentration. Dueker et al., published on 3 June 2026, isolated two antibodies with sarbecovirus and merbecovirus activity. The linked preprint describes eight vaccinated rhesus macaques and undetectable S2-directed serum cross-neutralisation.
milestones.set_by: Coronavirus neutralisation assay convention, applied by Dueker et al. in Figures 4–5; half-maximal neutralisation measurements and their units appear in the figures.

milestones.title: A coronavirus vaccine protects animals against challenge by a virus absent from its immunogens.
milestones.criterion: Vaccinated animals show protection after heterologous-virus challenge using the study's survival, weight-loss and viral-replication endpoints. Cohen et al., published on 5 August 2022, tested mosaic-8b against SARS-CoV, which was absent from its immunogens. In the survival cohorts, all six vaccinated K18-hACE2 mice survived 28 days after challenge; all six control mice reached endpoint criteria within four days. This establishes protection in that model and challenge.
milestones.set_by: Animal-challenge convention in coronavirus vaccine research, applied in the Caltech/NIAID study by Cohen et al.; the cited experiment concerns sarbecoviruses.
milestones.threshold_quote: evaluate survival, weight loss, and reduction or absence of viral replication as the primary metrics for vaccine efficacy

milestones.title: A coronavirus vaccine passes FDA IND review and is administered to human volunteers.
milestones.criterion: FDA review permits an Investigational New Drug application to proceed, and volunteers receive the candidate vaccine under the clinical protocol. Review covers preclinical findings, product quality, manufacturing and safety for human testing. The SpFN/ALFQ first-in-human study enrolled 29 adults between 7 April 2021 and 29 June 2021 and administered vaccine or placebo under protocol NCT04784767.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Vaccine Development – 101; the IND requirement is the US regulatory route.
milestones.threshold_quote: reasonably safe for testing of the vaccine to move forward

milestones.title: A coronavirus vaccine completes phase 1 assessment and elicits cross-sarbecovirus neutralisation.
milestones.criterion: A registered phase 1 study completes its safety and immunogenicity assessments and demonstrates vaccine-induced neutralisation beyond SARS-CoV-2. The SpFN/ALFQ report, published on 15 May 2024, assessed adverse events, antibodies and T cells: 20 participants received 25 μg, four received 50 μg and five received placebo. Doses were scheduled on days 1 and 29, with an optional third vaccination on day 181. Neutralisation of other clade 1 sarbecoviruses was detectable after two immunisations. Human protection was not an efficacy endpoint.
milestones.set_by: Walter Reed Army Institute of Research, registered SpFN/ALFQ protocol NCT04784767, as described in its trial publication; these assessments and doses are candidate-specific.
milestones.threshold_quote: Local and systemic reactogenicity, adverse events, binding and neutralising antibodies, and antigen-specific T-cell responses were quantified.

milestones.title: A coronavirus vaccine completes controlled phase 2 safety and dose–response assessment.
milestones.criterion: Randomised controlled phase 2 studies assess additional safety outcomes and the relationship between vaccine dose and immune response in populations relevant to intended use. FDA specifies these purposes without a universal numerical pass threshold. CEPI's portfolio dated 4 November 2026 places SK Bioscience's broadly protective betacoronavirus candidate at phase I/II; the portfolio does not report completed phase 2 outcomes.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, Vaccine Development – 101, phase 2 development stage.
milestones.threshold_quote: examine the relationship between the dose administered and the immune response

milestones.title: A coronavirus vaccine meets pivotal trial endpoints and has a commercial manufacturing process.
milestones.criterion: For the proposed breadth and duration indication, pivotal studies meet their regulator-agreed efficacy and safety endpoints, and the manufacturer develops a commercial manufacturing process supporting a Biologics License Application. This is FDA's stage immediately before licensing review. Numerical efficacy endpoints and any use of immune-response comparisons require agreement for the candidate and indication; the sources do not establish a common cross-betacoronavirus threshold.
milestones.set_by: US Food and Drug Administration, The Path for Vaccines, pre-application stage following phase 3.
milestones.threshold_quote: After phase 3 clinical trials meet specified milestones and the manufacturer develops a commercial manufacturing process, the manufacturer submits a BLA to the FDA.

not_found: No integrated external completion test specifying a pre-emergent coronavirus panel, clinical efficacy threshold and duration of protection was located.
No published pivotal human efficacy result supporting protection across sarbecoviruses and merbecoviruses was located.
The Cell Reports full text and CEPI's original detailed funding-call PDF could not be opened.
The ClinicalTrials.gov page opened without its endpoint record; SpFN/ALFQ protocol details were available in the trial publication.

results.finding: Two vaccine-elicited S2 stem-helix mAbs neutralized diverse sarbeco- and merbecoviruses, including MERS-CoV.
results.detail: Serum S2-directed cross-neutralization was undetectable, and the abstract does not report a 50% neutralization endpoint or specify a vaccine-absent virus for the isolated mAbs.
results.quote: two S2 stem-helix mAbs were identified from memory B cells. These bnAbs neutralized diverse sarbeco- and merbecoviruses, including MERS-CoV

results.finding: Two vaccine-elicited macaque mAbs (CHM-16, CHM-27) from 8 vaccinated rhesus macaques neutralized vaccine-absent SARS-CoV-1, WIV1 and Pang17 at IC50.
results.detail: The mAbs were isolated from memory B cells after heterologous SARS-CoV-2/MERS/HKU1/OC43 spike immunization; SARS-CoV-1, WIV1 and Pang17 were absent from the immunogens. Serum S2 cross-neutralization was undetectable.
results.quote: We found neutralization across all sarbecoviruses (SARS-CoV-1, SARS-CoV-2, WIV1, and Pang17) and merbecoviruses (MERS-CoV) tested (Figure 5a).
